stories.headline: Merz-Trump diplomatic rift over Iran war deepens as Steinmeier calls conflict 'illegal'
stories.summary: Chancellor Merz publicly criticized Trump's Iran war strategy as 'massive escalation' while President Steinmeier controversially declared the conflict 'völkerrechtswidrig' (illegal under international law). Foreign Minister Wadephul conducted damage control with US officials at G7 meetings.

stories.headline: Merz sparks controversy linking violence against women to migration
stories.summary: Chancellor Merz drew sharp criticism during a Bundestag session when he claimed that 'a significant portion' of Germany's 'exploding violence' comes from migrant groups. Opposition parties and Turkish community leaders condemned the remarks as inappropriate deflection from gender-based violence issues.

stories.headline: CDU wins Rheinland-Pfalz after 35 years as AfD achieves western breakthrough
stories.summary: The CDU secured victory in Rheinland-Pfalz with 31% of the vote, ending 35 years of SPD rule, while the AfD achieved its best-ever western German result with 19.5%. The SPD collapsed to just 25.9%, with CDU's Gordon Schnieder set to become the new minister-president in coalition talks with the SPD.

stories.headline: SPD faces leadership crisis as Klingbeil proposes major reforms amid election defeats
stories.summary: SPD faces mounting pressure on co-chairs Bärbel Bas and Lars Klingbeil after devastating losses in western state elections. Klingbeil delivered a major reform speech proposing to abolish joint taxation for married couples and raise taxes on high earners, while speculation grows about Boris Pistorius as potential replacement.

stories.headline: Defense Minister Pistorius strengthens Indo-Pacific ties on Asia tour, offers post-war Iran support
stories.summary: Defense Minister Boris Pistorius completed an eight-day tour of Japan, Singapore, and Australia, signing defense cooperation agreements and weapons deals. He stated Germany would be ready to help secure the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war ends, while staying for a controversial private vacation in Australia afterward.

stories.headline: Coalition tax reform negotiations intensify as Merz doesn't rule out VAT increase
stories.summary: Chancellor Merz did not rule out raising VAT from 19% to 21% during a parliamentary Q&A session, sparking opposition from business groups and some CDU politicians. The comments came amid ongoing coalition negotiations over tax reforms, including Klingbeil's proposals for income tax cuts and higher taxes on wealthy.

stories.headline: Green-CDU coalition talks begin in Baden-Württemberg after narrow election
stories.summary: Greens and CDU began sondierungsgespräche (exploratory talks) for a new coalition in Baden-Württemberg after the Greens narrowly won with 30.2% vs CDU's 29.7%. Both parties have exactly equal representation in the new parliament. Tensions remain from the campaign, with the CDU demanding strict confidentiality in negotiations.

stories.headline: AfD establishes itself as 20% party in western Germany, dominates among young voters
stories.summary: The AfD achieved breakthrough results in western German states, doubling its support to nearly 20% in both Baden-Württemberg and Rheinland-Pfalz. The party won the youth vote (18-44 age groups) and became the strongest party among workers. Analysis suggests AfD support is shifting from protest voting to conviction-based support.

stories.headline: Bundeswehr faces personnel crisis and equipment challenges amid expansion plans
stories.summary: The Bundeswehr struggles with personnel shortages, sexual misconduct cases, and equipment issues while trying to expand from 186,000 to 260,000 soldiers by 2035. A classified procurement document was leaked, leading to an officer's suspension. The military association calls for over 300,000 personnel and warns of a 'deterrence gap' against Russia.
